iron.clinical_target: Restore ferritin reserves and elevate hemoglobin synthesis

key_foods.name: Moringa (Drumstick) Leaves & Dal
key_foods.highlight: Exceptionally rich in non-heme iron and natural vitamin C

key_foods.name: Palak & Methi Saag (Spinach & Fenugreek)
key_foods.highlight: Cook in traditional iron kadai to boost bioavailability

key_foods.name: Sprouted Kala Chana (Black Chickpeas)
key_foods.highlight: Sprouting breaks down phytic acid to maximize absorption

key_foods.name: Garden Cress Seeds (Halim / Aliv)
key_foods.highlight: Traditional Indian postpartum powerhouse for rapid iron recovery

key_foods.name: Jaggery & Roasted Chana (Gur-Chana)
key_foods.highlight: Simple, accessible everyday Indian iron booster

key_foods.name: Country Chicken Liver / Mutton Liver
key_foods.highlight: Highest bioavailability heme iron, directly absorbed

bioavailability_rules: Always squeeze fresh Nimbu (lemon) or add Amla over green leafy vegetables — Vitamin C boosts non-heme iron absorption by up to 300%.
Avoid drinking Chai (tea) or Coffee within 1 hour before or after iron-rich meals, as tannins and polyphenols severely inhibit iron uptake.
Cook curries in cast-iron cookware (lohe ki kadai) to naturally leach dietary elemental iron into food.

key_foods.highlight: Boiled gently; daily Indian morning/bedtime staple

key_foods.name: Rohu / Katla / Hilsa / Pomfret Fish Curry
key_foods.highlight: Abundant cobalamin combined with heart-healthy omega-3 fats

key_foods.highlight: Essential for strict vegans who avoid dairy and poultry

bioavailability_rules: Lacto-vegetarians should consume at least 2 to 3 servings of dairy (curd, milk, paneer) distributed throughout the day.
If stomach acidity is low or antacids/metformin are taken regularly, consult a physician regarding sublingual methylcobalamin drops or B-complex.
Include fermented Indian preparations like idli, dosa, and kanji for beneficial gut microbiome synergy.

vitamin_d.clinical_target: Normalize circulating 25(OH)D levels and bone mineralization

key_foods.name: Sun-Exposed Button / Shiitake Mushrooms
key_foods.highlight: Exposing sliced mushrooms to midday sunlight for 30 mins generates Vitamin D2

key_foods.name: FSSAI Fortified Milk & Ghee (+F logo)
key_foods.highlight: Nationally fortified staples compliant with FSSAI standards

key_foods.name: Fortified Cooking Oils (Mustard / Soy / Sunflower)
key_foods.highlight: Look for the blue +F fortified logo on retail oil pouches

key_foods.name: Whole Desi Egg Yolks
key_foods.highlight: Natural lipid-soluble cholecalciferol vehicle

key_foods.name: Mackerel (Bangda) / Sardines (Tarli)
key_foods.highlight: Affordable coastal Indian oily fish packed with natural Vitamin D3

bioavailability_rules: Get 15–25 minutes of direct sunlight on arms, legs, and face between 11:00 AM and 1:30 PM without sunscreen, 3–4 times weekly for endogenous dermal synthesis.
Vitamin D is fat-soluble: always consume dietary sources with healthy fats (ghee, cold-pressed mustard oil, or whole milk) for intestinal micelle incorporation.
In severe deficiency (serum < 20 ng/mL), clinical weekly cholecalciferol (60,000 IU) supplementation under doctor supervision is standard protocol.

calcium.clinical_target: Maintain skeletal density, prevent osteopenia, and stabilize neuromuscular firing

key_foods.name: Ragi / Finger Millet (Roti, Mudde, Porridge)
key_foods.highlight: Highest calcium content among all cereals — over 10x that of rice or wheat

key_foods.name: White & Black Sesame Seeds (Til Laddu / Chutney)
key_foods.highlight: Ancient Indian superseed delivering concentrated organic calcium and lignans

key_foods.name: Fresh Indian Curd (Dahi)
key_foods.highlight: High bioavailability with bio-active peptides

key_foods.name: Moringa Leaves / Drumsticks
key_foods.highlight: Substantially lower oxalate levels compared to raw spinach, boosting absorption

key_foods.name: Tofu / Paneer
key_foods.highlight: Calcium-set tofu or fresh milk paneer for muscle and bone repair

key_foods.name: Small Bone-in Fish (Anchovies / Nethili)
key_foods.highlight: Consuming edible soft bones provides intact hydroxyapatite matrix

bioavailability_rules: Soak millets and pulses for 6–8 hours and discard the soaking water to reduce phytates and antinutrients.
Pair calcium intake with adequate Vitamin D; without Vitamin D, only 10–15% of dietary calcium is absorbed in the gut.
Spread calcium intake across multiple meals rather than a single large dose, as intestinal fractional absorption declines above 500 mg per meal.

zinc.clinical_target: Enhance mucosal barrier repair, wound healing velocity, and T-cell response

key_foods.name: Pumpkin Seeds (Kaddu ke Beej) & Watermelon Seeds
key_foods.highlight: Easiest everyday Indian seed snack; lightly roast with rock salt

key_foods.name: Kabuli Chana / Rajma / Moong Dal
key_foods.highlight: Soaked and sprouted to unlock bioavailable chelated zinc

key_foods.name: Cashews & Almonds (Kaju & Badam)
key_foods.highlight: Traditional Indian morning soaked nuts with healthy monounsaturated fats

key_foods.name: Whole Bajra (Pearl Millet) Khichdi / Roti
key_foods.highlight: Traditional winter grain rich in zinc, iron, and dietary fiber

key_foods.name: Mutton / Chicken Thigh (Curry)
key_foods.highlight: High bio-potency zinc with no phytic acid interference

bioavailability_rules: Sprouting (ankuran) pulses and fermenting batters (like idli/dosa) activates phytase enzyme, degrading phytates and doubling zinc absorption.
Avoid taking high-dose iron supplements at the exact same meal as zinc, as they compete for the divalent metal transporter (DMT-1).
Incorporate sulfur-containing alliums (garlic and onions) in curry bases, which have been proven to enhance zinc bioaccessibility from pulses.

folate.clinical_target: Restore normal RBC mean corpuscular volume (MCV) and homocysteine clearance

key_foods.highlight: Uncooked raw sprouted moong preserves heat-sensitive natural polyglutamates

key_foods.name: Methi (Fenugreek) & Palak Saag
key_foods.highlight: Steam or light saute rather than prolonged boiling to prevent folate breakdown

key_foods.name: Toor Dal / Chana Dal / Masoor Dal
key_foods.highlight: Core foundation of daily Indian thali, providing steady folate and protein

key_foods.name: Bhindi (Okra / Lady Finger Curry)
key_foods.highlight: Cooked with mustard seeds and amchur/lemon for optimal nutrient preservation

key_foods.name: Papaya & Mosambi (Sweet Lime) / Oranges
key_foods.highlight: Fresh seasonal citrus fruits rich in active L-methylfolate and vitamin C

key_foods.name: Desi Eggs
key_foods.highlight: Synergistic folate and B12 combination in egg yolk

bioavailability_rules: Folate is highly water-soluble and heat-sensitive; avoid over-boiling vegetables in open pots for extended durations. Steam or pressure-cook with minimal water.
Include at least one portion of raw or lightly steamed salad (sprouts, cucumber, tomatoes with lemon) daily.
Women of reproductive age planning pregnancy should maintain optimal folate to prevent neural tube defects.

vitamin_a.clinical_target: Support rhodopsin regeneration in retina and corneal epithelial health

key_foods.highlight: Packed with provitamin A beta-carotene; cooked with milk/ghee for maximum uptake

key_foods.name: Kaddu / Pumpkin Curry (Sitaphal / Petha)
key_foods.highlight: Gentle on digestion and rich in alpha- and beta-carotene

key_foods.name: Ripe Alphonso / Kesar Mango / Papaya
key_foods.highlight: Indian summer delight bursting with active carotenoids and antioxidants

key_foods.name: Moringa Leaf Bhaji / Drumstick Curry
key_foods.highlight: One of the densest green leafy sources of provitamin A

key_foods.name: Pure Cow Desi Ghee & Fortified Milk
key_foods.highlight: Provides preformed retinol and the vital lipid matrix needed to absorb carotenoids

key_foods.name: Egg Yolk & Liver
key_foods.highlight: Direct, preformed retinol ready for immediate metabolic use

bioavailability_rules: Beta-carotene from carrots, papaya, and leafy greens is fat-soluble — always consume them with a small amount of dietary fat (ghee, mustard oil, or curd).
Light cooking or pureeing breaks vegetable cell walls, increasing carotenoid bioavailability by up to 400% compared to raw fibrous chunks.
Ensure concurrent Zinc adequacy, as zinc is mandatory for hepatic synthesis of Retinol-Binding Protein (RBP) to transport Vitamin A through bloodstream.
